pages.title: Football — FIFA World Cup 2026 and SAFF Women's

facts.text: 23rd edition, 11 June–19 July 2026; hosts USA, Canada, Mexico — ⚠ first with three hosts
facts.head: FIFA World Cup 2026

facts.text: 48 teams (up from 32), 104 matches, 12 groups of 4; top 2 + best 8 third-placed advance; Round of 32 introduced for first time
facts.head: FIFA World Cup 2026

facts.text: Opening: Estadio Azteca, Mexico City; final: MetLife Stadium, USA
facts.head: FIFA World Cup 2026

facts.text: ⚠ Mexico first to host three times (1970, 1986, 2026); defending champion Argentina
facts.head: FIFA World Cup 2026

facts.text: FIFA: est. 1904, Zurich; President Gianni Infantino
facts.head: FIFA World Cup 2026

facts.text: India won record 6th title beating defending champions Bangladesh 3–1 in final (6 June 2026) at Fatorda Stadium, Margao, Goa; unbeaten — 18 goals scored, 1 conceded

facts.text: Event: Asian U-20 Athletics (Hong Kong, 28–31 May); Result: India 2nd — 19 medals (10G, 5S, 4B); China 1st (25 — 14G, 9S, 2B), Japan 3rd (18 — 5G, 5S, 8B); venue Kai Tak Youth Sports Ground; formerly Asian Junior Championships (Asian Athletics Association — 1973, Seoul; AFI President Bahadur Singh Sagoo)
facts.head: Table

facts.text: Event: FIH Women's Nations Cup (Auckland); Result: India won (2nd time), beat New Zealand 2–0 — goals Navneet Kaur, Sunelita Toppo; qualified for FIH Pro League; conceded no goal (FIH — 1924, Lausanne, President Tayyab Ikram)
facts.head: Table

facts.text: Event: U-18 Hockey Asia Cup (Kakamigahara, Japan); Result: India beat Japan 4–1; Ashish Tani Purty hat-trick; captain Ketan Kushwaha; ₹3 lakh per player from Hockey India (est. 2009, President Dilip Tirkey); women won bronze (3–0 vs South Korea)
facts.head: Table

facts.text: Event: U-17 Asian Wrestling (Da Nang, Vietnam); Result: Indian women — medals in all 10 categories (2G, 3S, 5B); gold — Diksha (43 kg), Garima (73 kg); 28–31 May; by United World Wrestling (est. 1912 as FILA)
facts.head: Table

facts.text: Event: ISSF Junior World Championship (Suhl, Germany, 16–26 June); Result: India 1st — 25 medals (7G, 8S, 10B); Individual Neutral Athletes 2nd (14), Italy 3rd (10); 84-member team; 800+ shooters, 70 countries (ISSF — 1907, Munich; NRAI 1951)
facts.head: Table

facts.text: Event: World Rowing Cup III (Lucerne, 27 June); Result: ⚠ India's first-ever gold — Havildar Lakshya and Havildar Ujwal Kumar Singh, Lightweight Men's Double Sculls, 6:26.09 — in their first international event (Indian Army pair; Olympic race distance 2,000 m)
facts.head: Table

facts.text: Event: 2nd Asian Relay Championships (Shaoxing, China); Result: Women's 4×100 m gold (43.85 s) — Shrabani Nanda, Sneha Sanuvalli, Sudeshna Shivankar, Tamanna; beat China, Thailand; mixed 4×400 m silver (M.R. Poovamma, Neeru Pathak, Teerthesh P. Shetty, Bharat Sridhar); mixed 4×100 m bronze (Animesh Kujur, Pranav Gurav, Tamanna, Sneha Sanuvalli); Chandigarh hosts 2027
facts.head: Table

facts.text: R. Praggnanandhaa: ⚠ first Indian to win Norway Chess (Oslo, 5 June 2026) — 18 points, one ahead of Wesley So (USA); beat Vincent Keymer in last round; beat World No. 1 Magnus Carlsen twice in classical games; GM since 2018
facts.head: Chess

facts.text: Savitha Shri Bhasker (IM): gold, women's Asian Individual Chess Championship 2026, Ulaanbaatar (29 May–7 June) — 7.5/9, on tie-break; qualifies for 2027 FIDE Women's World Cup; open — Kang Xiangrui (China); Swiss format; 21st open / 27th women's edition (Asian Chess Federation — 1978, Al Ain)
facts.head: Chess

facts.text: Viswanathan Anand: SJFI Gold Medal (instituted 2019) — presented by K. Srikkanth at Madras Cricket Club; 6th recipient after Gavaskar, Vijay Amritraj, Prakash Padukone, P.T. Usha, Milkha Singh; India's first GM (1988); first Khel Ratna recipient; FIDE Deputy President; 5-time world champion
facts.head: Chess

facts.text: FIDE: est. 1924, Lausanne; President Arkady Dvorkovich
facts.head: Chess

facts.text: SAI–University of Tsukuba (Japan): 3-year MoU — signed by Manjushree Dayanand and Kyosuke Nagata; via TIAS 2.0 — athletics, archery, table tennis, swimming, judo; builds on 2016 India–Japan sports pact and 2018 SAI–Tsukuba tie-up (SAI est. 1984; Tsukuba est. 1973)
facts.head: Sports cooperation

facts.text: Person: Jaspal Rana; Fact: Shooting coach, died 12 June 2026 in New Delhi aged 49 (fell ill returning from ISSF World Cup, Germany); 15 CWG medals (9G, 4S, 2B); equalled WR in 25 m Centre Fire Pistol; 3 golds at 2006 Doha Asian Games; coached Manu Bhaker (2 bronzes, Paris 2024); Arjuna 1994, Padma Shri 1997, Dronacharya 2020
facts.head: Table

facts.text: Person: Smriti Mandhana; Fact: ⚠ Only Indian in inaugural TIME100 Most Influential People in Sports list — Titans category (with Ronaldo, Haaland, Temba Bavuma); categories Leaders, Icons, Innovators, Titans; 2-time ICC Women's Cricketer of the Year (TIME est. 1923)
facts.head: Table

facts.text: Person: Lionel Messi; Fact: Princess of Asturias Award for Sports 2026
